description: Built-in dictionary library ids in precedence order: when two enabled built-in libraries list the same spoken form, the one earlier here supplies the rule, and this order decides which terms fill the on-device AI cleanup glossary. The first eleven are the order Scribe 0.4.3 composed them in (category, then name, ordinal and case-insensitive), frozen as ids so a rename or a new category never moves a library. Append a new built-in at the end; never reorder or remove an id. When a built-in stops shipping, keep its id in "order" and add it to "retired", the only way an id in "order" may be missing from the shipped libraries. Windows keeps the same lists in Scribe.Core.Libraries.LibraryPrecedence (BuiltInOrder and RetiredBuiltInIds), and LibraryPrecedenceTests fails until they agree. Custom libraries come after every built-in, in the order of their file names.
